messages:
incident-bot: Pager alert — elevated 5xx and gateway_timeouts observed for /v1/generate in eu-west-1. 5xx rate jumped to ~18% over 5m, primary error classes: 504 gateway timeout / 502 bad gateway. Alert ID RED-INC-3167894321. Paging infra oncall.

Alex Chen: oncall infra here, ack. looking at gateway and prefix-cache graphs now. eviction/sec on prefix-cache-shard-7 is ~4200 (baseline ~20). also seeing cache write errors and backlog on shard 7.

Priya Sinha: runtime — noticed a TTL churn pattern and compaction job kicked ~2m before spike, might be a TTL-race + compaction interaction causing mass evictions. spikes line up with logrotate/compaction window.

Matt Gupta: support — multiple customers reporting 502/504s (acme-inc, finserv-co). initial impact estimate: ~3 customers affected, ~12k failed requests in last 10m. customers seeing request timeouts and retries.

Alex Chen: grabbing logs from shard7, excerpt:
```
[2026-03-15T09:12:10Z] prefixd[shard7]: eviction_loop: freed 12MB entries_wait=0.12s
[2026-03-15T09:12:14Z] gateway[gw-13]: upstream_error: 504 timeout waiting for cache miss read (backend-read 12001ms)
[2026-03-15T09:12:17Z] prefixd[shard7]: mem_pressure: reclaiming, candidates=4823
```

Alex Chen: mitigation plan proposals — 1) flip cache bypass on shard-7 to reduce eviction pressure and let requests cold-read from backing store, 2) increase backing-store read concurrency to absorb thundering herd, 3) route a small % of /v1/generate traffic to eu-north-1 as temporary fallback, 4) roll prefixd on shard7 one at a time to clear any leaked state.

Priya Sinha: agreed. do bypass first and scale backing reads. I'll also disable the compaction job window for the next hour to avoid repeats.

Alex Chen: executing bypass now:
```
# temporary bypass to avoid cache churn
redwoodctl cache set-bypass --shard shard-7 --duration 30m --reason "eviction storm"
```

deploy-bot: redwoodctl: cache bypass requested by Alex Chen for shard-7 — queued.

Alex Chen: bypass applied ✅. enabling increased read concurrency to the backing store (scale from 64 -> 256 drivers).

Priya Sinha: disabling compaction/maintenance window for affected shards:
```
# disable compaction window
redwoodctl maintenance set-window --component prefixd --disable --duration 60m
```

Infra SRE: starting rolling restart of prefixd on shard-7 nodes, one at a time, to ensure no long-lived corruption. doing safe drain -> restart -> healthcheck.

Alex Chen: also added a short routing override to send 20% of /v1/generate traffic to eu-north-1 while we verify error rates dropping:
```
redwoodctl routing override --route /v1/generate --from eu-west-1 --to eu-north-1 --percentage 20 --duration 45m
```

Matt Gupta: customer comms — sending proactive note to acme-inc and finserv-co that we are investigating and have temporary mitigations in place; offering workaround (retry/backoff) and will follow up with timeline.

Priya Sinha: monitoring graphs — 5xx rate dropped from 18% -> 3% within 3m of bypass + routing override. gateway timeouts reduced. still watching tail latencies on cold reads.

Alex Chen: rolling restarts finished, healthchecks green. continuing to watch for error resurfacing.

Infra SRE: left one action item: run consistency check on shard-7 keys to detect any potential corruption from compaction race. will schedule low-priority background job now.

Matt Gupta: noted customer impact and actions in ticket INC-3167894321; CS will do follow-up tomorrow for any lingering requests.

Priya Sinha: handing incident to Alex Chen for post-incident monitoring and follow-up (next 8 hours). I'll draft a short blameless postmortem template with timeline + RCA pointers (TTL race + compaction interaction + insufficient eviction backpressure controls).

Alex Chen: thanks — will own the follow-up. immediate mitigation still in place (bypass + routing override). will update this thread if anything regresses. :thumbsup:

Customer Success: customers notified. no new escalations as of last check.

Priya Sinha: postmortem link (WIP): https://redwood.incidents/INC-3167894321/postmortem — adding logs and action items.

Alex Chen: handoff complete. leaving monitoring watches active. incident cleared for active pager; oncall will still monitor.
